correctness.rationale: Every left ideal is \(M_U\), with \(M_U\cap M_W=M_{U+W}\). For \(n=2\), distinct lines span the whole space, so the graph is edgeless. For \(n\ge3\), the known \(q+1\) lines in a two-dimensional subspace dominate and their ideals form a clique; the published ordinary lower bound therefore proves the same total minimum. Paired domination equals that even clique size for odd \(q\), while even \(q\) forces one more vertex and an external line supplies a \(q+2\)-clique.

originality.rationale: Akbari and Nikandish's Theorem 14 already proves \(\gamma=q+1\) for the same left-ideal graph using the exact \(q+1\) lines in a two-dimensional subspace that the package reuses. For \(n\ge3\), any two of those lines span only that proper two-space, so their corresponding ideals intersect and the published minimum witness is automatically a clique. Total domination therefore costs nothing beyond the published ordinary minimum, while paired domination is only the parity correction. The \(n=2\) edgeless boundary follows immediately from the same subspace-intersection formula.
